title: Microfluidic Platform for Measuring Neutrophil Chemotaxis from Unprocessed Whole Blood
protocol: Use standard photolithographic techniques to fabricate the master mold wafer in a class 1,000 clean room.
Pattern the first 3-µm-thin epoxy-based negative photoresist layer to define migration channels according to manufacturer instructions.
Pattern the second 50-µm-thick layer to define cell-loading and chemokine chambers.
Mix PDMS (20 g) with initiator (2 g) for 5 min using a plastic fork in a large plastic weighing tray.
Pour mixed PDMS onto the patterned wafer.
Place mold with poured PDMS into a vacuum desiccator for degassing for 1 hr.
Bake and cure PDMS microfluidic devices at 65 °C for at least 3 hr in an oven.
Punch out central WBLCs using a puncher with a tip diameter of 1.5 mm.
Punch out whole donut-shaped devices using a puncher with a tip diameter of 5.0 mm.
Remove particles from donut devices using adhesive tape.
Rinse a 12-well plate with deionized water and dry it with nitrogen.
Place the rinsed and dried 12-well plate in an oven at 60 °C for 5 min.
Oxygen plasma treat the 12-well plate twice, each for 35 sec: once alone and once again with the donut devices.
Carefully place the bonded devices into the wells of the 12-well plate using tweezers.
Bake the plate with bonded devices on a hot plate at 80 °C for 10 min.
Prime microfluidic devices immediately after oxygen plasma treatment when they are hydrophilic.
Create chemoattractant solution by mixing 5 μl fMLP stock (10 µM) with 5 μl fibronectin stock (1 mg/ml) and 490 μl HBSS.
Slowly pipette the chemoattractant solution into WBLC using a gel loading tip.
Pipette an additional 20 μl of the chemoattractant around the outside of the device.
Place the plate in a desiccator for 15 min.
Apply vacuum to instill the chemoattractant solution into the side-channels and allow displaced air to diffuse out through PDMS.
Remove plate from desiccator and confirm wetting of device channels under microscope.
Wash WBLC and outside of the device thoroughly to remove excess chemoattractant solution.
Fill a 1-ml syringe with PBS, add a 30 G blunt needle tip to the syringe.
Gently insert the needle tip into the center of the donut hole.
Gently push 100 μl of PBS into the hole so that a droplet forms on top of the device.
Tilt plate and pipette 1 ml of PBS around device so that the liquid collects at the bottom of the well.
Aspirate the liquid.
Repeat process for a total of 3 times using fresh buffer solution.
Fill each well with media until the tops of the devices are submerged under liquid.
Let the devices sit for 15 min to allow gradient to stabilize.
Using gel loading tips, slowly pipette 2 μl of blood (or isolated neutrophils) into each whole blood loading chamber (WBLC).
Wash hands with water and soap and dry the skin for finger prick blood collection.
Prepare anti-coagulant/stain stock solution by adding 1 ml HBSS + 0.2% HSA and 10 µl Hoechst stain (32.4 μM) to heparin blood collection tube.
Prick the finger using a SurgiLance safety lancet (2.2-mm depth, 22 G).
Wipe away the first drop of blood and collect 50 μl of blood in Eppendorf tube containing the stock anti-coagulant and Hoechst fluorescent stain solution.
Gently mix the collected blood with the stock solution.
Incubate the blood and Hoechst stain for 10 min to allow for nucleus fluorescent staining.
Run sample within 1 hr of blood collection.
Draw 10 ml of peripheral, venous blood into tubes containing 33 USP heparin.
Add 50 µl of venous blood to media and Hoechst stain as previously described.
Incubate the blood and Hoechst stain for 10 min to allow for nucleus fluorescent staining.
Run sample within 1 hr of blood collection.

Use sterile techniques to isolate neutrophils from the 10 ml venous whole blood sample using Hetastarch (6% w/v) density gradient followed by a negative selection magnetic bead isolation kit following the manufacturer's protocol.
Resuspend the final aliquot of neutrophils at a concentration of 4,000 cells/µl in 1X HBSS + 0.2% human serum albumin.
Keep cells at 37 °C until ready to run the experiment.
Set up biochamber temperature to 37 °C.
Set up biochamber humidity to 80%.
Set up biochamber CO2 level to 5%.
Start imaging immediately using time-lapse imaging on a microscope at 10X or higher magnification.
Manually track at least 50 neutrophils in each sample.
Count the cells entering the FCC over time.
Calculate neutrophil velocities in the channel between WBLC and FCC using ImageJ (NIH).
Quantify directionality of neutrophils by counting the number of cells that pass the bifurcation.
Calculate the ratio between the number of cells that turn toward the FCC and cells that exit the device.
